operations.comment: ; Bases Loaded 3 (NES, MMC3) -- commented ca65 source, rebuilt byte-identically
; from the local ROM image. See the file-level notes below for conventions.
; Layout: one ca65 segment reproduces the whole iNES file in physical order (header, 32 PRG
; banks of 8 KiB, 16 CHR banks of 8 KiB). Each classified region keeps its phase-1 (pass-003)
; header line '; <Kind>; <Provenance>; physical <start>..<end>'; code regions add the PRG bank,
; and '(continues)' marks a code region that directly continues the previous one in the same
; assembler block. The two bytes outside classified regions (bank 28) stay raw .incbin with an 'Unknown' note.
; Unreferenced code: banks 0/4 hold copies of the bank 2 field code, bank 6 an older variant of
; bank 16, and routines described as 'uncalled (no caller found)' have no static reference.
; Banking (MMC3, PRG mode 0): banks 30 and 31 are fixed at $C000/$E000. Switchable code
; always runs with an even bank at $8000 and the following odd bank at $A000, because the
; far-call helper FarCall maps banks N and N+1 together. Label values are CPU addresses in
; that context, so labels in different banks may share an address.
; Far calls: callers load FarCallIndex ($3B) with an even byte offset and FarCallBank ($3C)
; with an even bank number, then JSR FarCall. FarCall reads a 16-bit routine pointer from
; offset $8001+index of the target bank (the word table right after that bank's id byte),
; calls it, and restores the previous bank pair. Each pointer table (FarCallTable_NN) is
; listed in source as .addr entries naming the target routines.
; Naming conventions: routine labels are CamelCase; cheap local labels (@loop, @skip, @done,
; @return) are mechanical branch targets inside one routine; 'Owner_Cont'/'Owner_Return'
; labels are shared entry points reached from another routine. Every routine, RAM variable and
; referenced ROM table has a descriptive name; where only the mechanical role is known the name
; describes that role and the comment states what is uncertain. Statements such as
; 'probably' or 'appears to' are inferences from code and runtime traces, not proofs.
; read: id byte of the bank mapped at $8000 (BankIdNN)
; read: FarCall routine pointer table of the bank at $8000
